source.authors: Malik HR, Bertolesi GE, McFarlane S
source.title: TRPM8 thermosensation in poikilotherms mediates both skin colour and locomotor performance responses to cold temperature

value: cold response: skin lightening by melanosome aggregation within 20-30 min after a switch from 24 °C to 6 °C
method: whole-animal cold-exposure assay: stage 42/43 tadpoles moved from a 24 °C to a 6 °C incubator; melanosome aggregation scored as a pigmentation index from images; TRP channel pharmacology (agonists and antagonists in the water)
conditions: stage 42/43 tadpoles, n = 8-10 per condition in 2-3 independent experiments, in petri dishes inside chambers (40 x 20 x 25 cm) lit by fluorescent bulbs and placed in a 24 °C or 6 °C incubator (Methods); the only cold temperature tested for the main response is 6 °C, so no threshold or tuning curve is given here; a behavioural-physiological response of the whole animal, not a recording from thermoreceptors
quote: Switching the tadpoles from 24 °C to 6 °C induced a significant aggregation of melanosomes within 20–30 min, resulting in skin lightening as seen by a reduced pigmentation index (Fig. 2b).
note: Cold sensing read through a skin-colour response in the larva. The authors tie it to TRPM8 (next record). The quote is rebuilt from two consecutive tool segments confirmed on a second pass. Xenopus laevis (Daudin, 1802): heading of the Amphibian Species of the World account (amphibiansoftheworld.amnh.org/Amphibia/Anura/Pipidae/Xenopus/Xenopus-laevis), which also notes that Measey and Channing (2003) suggested the nominal species is a species complex. source.authors: Malik HR, Bertolesi GE, McFarlane S
source.title: TRPM8 thermosensation in poikilotherms mediates both skin colour and locomotor performance responses to cold temperature

value: cold response needs a TRPM8 channel: the TRPM8 agonist WS12 mimics cooling and a TRPM8 antagonist blocks it
method: whole-animal cold-exposure assay: stage 42/43 tadpoles moved from a 24 °C to a 6 °C incubator; melanosome aggregation scored as a pigmentation index from images; TRP channel pharmacology (agonists and antagonists in the water)
conditions: stage 42/43 tadpoles, n = 8-10 per condition in 2-3 independent experiments, in petri dishes inside chambers (40 x 20 x 25 cm) lit by fluorescent bulbs and placed in a 24 °C or 6 °C incubator (Methods); the only cold temperature tested for the main response is 6 °C, so no threshold or tuning curve is given here; a behavioural-physiological response of the whole animal, not a recording from thermoreceptors; antagonist PF05105679 blocked cold-induced aggregation in a dose-dependent manner and had no effect at 24 °C (Results)
quote: Temperature-induced melanosome aggregation is mimicked by the Trpm8 agonist menthol (WS12) and blocked by a Trpm8 antagonist.
note: Contrary results in the same paper: the TRPA1 agonist AITC had no effect on skin pigmentation at any concentration tested, and the TRPM4 blocker CBA did not affect cooling-induced lightening (Results, tool summary). Pharmacological evidence for TRPM8 involvement, not a receptor-level recording. Xenopus laevis (Daudin, 1802): heading of the Amphibian Species of the World account (amphibiansoftheworld.amnh.org/Amphibia/Anura/Pipidae/Xenopus/Xenopus-laevis), which also notes that Measey and Channing (2003) suggested the nominal species is a species complex. source.title: TRPM8 thermosensation in poikilotherms mediates both skin colour and locomotor performance responses to cold temperature

value: locomotor performance of tadpoles is lower at 6 °C than at 24 °C
method: swimming recorded for 1 min every 5 min over 30 min at 24 °C and 6 °C
conditions: stage 45/46 tadpoles, n = 8, 2 independent experiments (Fig. 5 legend); locomotor apparatus not described in the text reached; a whole-animal response to cold, not a thermoreceptor measurement
quote: Cooling also induces a reduction in the locomotor performance.
note: The Results sentence reads 'Indeed, the locomotor performance at stage 45/46 differed significantly between tadpoles at 24 °C and 6 °C (Fig. 5b, c).' and gives no figure for the size of the reduction in the text read. source.authors: Metzen MG, Huang CG, Chacron MJ
source.title: Descending pathways generate perception of and neural responses to weak sensory input

value: behavioural detection threshold 8.8 ± 1.1 % contrast (mean ± SEM), range 1.1-27.6 %, n = 35 fish
method: behavioural detection: the stimulus is a 5 Hz sinusoidal amplitude modulation of the fish's own electric organ discharge (EOD) whose depth rose linearly from 0 to 100%; the response is a rise in EOD frequency, and the threshold is the lowest contrast at which EOD frequency left the central 95% of its unstimulated distribution
conditions: fish immobilized with intramuscular tubocurarine (0.1-0.5 mg), held in a tank of home-tank water and respired by a flow of oxygenated water through the mouth (the EOD is neurogenic and unaffected by curare); wave-type species; threshold is a contrast (modulation depth) of the animal's own field, not an absolute field strength in mV/cm
quote: We found that fish could reliably detect weak contrasts as evidenced from low detection thresholds (n = 35 fish, 8.8% ± 1.1%, min: 1.1%, max: 27.6%, Fig 2B, bottom, inset).
note: The same paper reports that electroreceptor afferent thresholds from phase locking (9.1 ± 1.1 %) matched this behavioural value while thresholds computed from firing rate were much higher (38.2 ± 3.1 %), so the behaviour tracks the timing code (Results, tool summary). Apteronotus leptorhynchus (Ellis 1912): 'Valid as Apteronotus leptorhynchus (Ellis 1912)' in Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes (researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=30099), Apteronotidae. source.authors: Metzen MG, Huang CG, Chacron MJ
source.title: Descending pathways generate perception of and neural responses to weak sensory input

value: behavioural detection threshold rose to 34.2 ± 6.3 % contrast after lidocaine inactivation of descending feedback (control 12.2 ± 2.3 %)
method: behavioural detection: the stimulus is a 5 Hz sinusoidal amplitude modulation of the fish's own electric organ discharge (EOD) whose depth rose linearly from 0 to 100%; the response is a rise in EOD frequency, and the threshold is the lowest contrast at which EOD frequency left the central 95% of its unstimulated distribution; descending feedback pharmacologically inactivated with lidocaine
conditions: fish immobilized with intramuscular tubocurarine (0.1-0.5 mg), held in a tank of home-tank water and respired by a flow of oxygenated water through the mouth (the EOD is neurogenic and unaffected by curare); wave-type species; threshold is a contrast (modulation depth) of the animal's own field, not an absolute field strength in mV/cm; lidocaine group N = 15 fish, saline vehicle control N = 10 (Methods, tool summary); the n behind the 12.2 % control value is not stated separately
quote: EOD frequency only became significantly different from baseline for much larger contrasts than under control conditions, leading to significantly larger behavioral detection threshold values (control: 12.2% ± 2.3%; lidocaine: 34.2% ± 6.3%, … Fig 6C, brown boxes).
note: Limiting context for the 8.8 % threshold: it depends on intact descending feedback. Treatment effect, not the intact animal's threshold. The omitted statistic is a Wilcoxon sign rank test, p = 6.1 × 10−5. Apteronotus leptorhynchus (Ellis 1912): 'Valid as Apteronotus leptorhynchus (Ellis 1912)' in Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes (researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/ichthyology/catalog/fishcatget.asp?spid=30099), Apteronotidae. eye: whole animal (ear and lateral line, behavioural startle)

source.authors: Holgate A, White PR, Leighton TG, Kemp PS
source.title: Applying appropriate frequency criteria to advance acoustic behavioural guidance systems for fish

value: startle thresholds (25% of fish): 123 dB at 250 Hz, 128 dB at 400 Hz, 145 dB at 600 Hz, 145 dB at 800 Hz re 1 µPa
method: behavioural startle assay: 120 ms tones at six frequencies (250-2000 Hz) and four sound pressure levels (115-145 dB re 1 µPa); deterrence threshold = the SPL at which 25% of the tested fish startled, from a logistic fit
conditions: goldfish n = 80 (mean standard length 64.0 mm, SD 5.3; mass 10.2 g, SD 2.4), each fish used in one trial only, held (constrained) within a white polyethylene test cylinder submerged in a large water tank (8 x 8 x 5 m); a startle (deterrence) threshold, not an auditory threshold; thresholds were fitted for 250, 400, 600 and 800 Hz only, and 1000 and 2000 Hz were left out because the logistic relationship was not significant
quote: The SPL eliciting a startle response for 25% of the population at 250, 400, 600, and 800 Hz was 123, 128, 145 and 145 dB re 1 μPa, respectively.
note: Behavioural startle levels are far above the AEP hearing thresholds the authors compare them with. At least 25% of fish startled only at 250 to 800 Hz (Results). Carassius auratus (Linnaeus, 1758): FishBase summary page (fishbase.se/summary/271) lists it as the scientific name of the goldfish, Cyprinidae; the Catalog of Fishes page for it was not reached. Licence: the nature.com PDF read states Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 and Crossref gives https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0. The PDF carries '© The Author(s) 2023, corrected publication 2024'; the Author Correction notice itself (10.1038/s41598-024-56278-w) could not be opened. The abstract gives differences of 47.1 dB (250 Hz) and 76 dB (600 Hz) from published hearing thresholds while the Results give 43 and 74 dB (AEP comparison), a mismatch in the paper.
